These compounds are known to interact with enzymes involved in drug metabolism and detoxification pathways. The high scores from the prediction models indicate a plausible biological connection, though the exact mechanism of interaction remains to be elucidated. The evidence supports a possible role of Equine Botulinum Neurotoxin C Immune FAB2 in modulating the activity of UDP-glucuronosyltransferase 2B15, likely through the regulation of CDK3/Cyclin E. However, further experimental validation is needed to confirm this relationship and understand the underlying molecular mechanisms.
